memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Early the next morning Abraham got up and loaded his donkey. He took with him two of his servants and his son Isaac. When he had cut enough wood for the burnt offering, he set out for the place God had told him about. - Gen 22:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Early the next morning Abraham got up." There is so much contained in that simple line. Abraham did not delay, did not argue, did not spend days trying to talk God out of it. He rose early and began to obey the hardest command he had ever received. His obedience was prompt, even in the face of unimaginable pain.

We should not imagine this was easy for him. The night before must have been agonising - sleepless, tearful, wrestling. Yet when morning came, Abraham got up and obeyed. His prompt obedience did not mean he felt no pain; it meant his trust in God ran deeper than his pain.

Notice the quiet, deliberate steps: loading the donkey, cutting the wood, gathering the servants and his son. Each action was a small act of obedience, one after another. Sometimes faithfulness looks like simply doing the next thing, even when our hearts are breaking.

This is a searching example for us. When God makes something clear, do we obey promptly, or do we delay, negotiate, and look for exits? Delayed obedience often becomes disobedience. Abraham teaches us to rise early and take the next faithful step, even through tears, trusting the God who commands. "I will hasten and not delay to obey your commands" (Ps 119:60). What is the next step of obedience God is asking of you today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you obey God promptly, or delay and look for exits?
- What is the next small step of obedience God is asking of you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me the prompt obedience of Abraham, who rose early to do the hardest thing. Even when my heart is breaking, help me take the next faithful step, trusting You more than I fear the pain.
Amen.
